results.title: CMS Transmittal 1875 - Consultation service codes no longer recognized for Medicare payment
results.text:
# Medicare consultation code elimination, January 1, 2010

## Policy change

Effective January 1, 2010, Medicare stopped recognizing consultation service codes 99241-99245 and 99251-99255 for Part B payment under the physician fee schedule. The change was applied budget-neutrally across inpatient and office/outpatient settings, with limited exceptions for telehealth consultation G-codes.

## Rationale

CMS restructured evaluation and management (E/M) payment. The transmittal states that the agency increased the work relative value units (RVUs) for new and established office visits and increased payment for initial hospital and nursing facility visits. These increased values were also carried into practice expense and malpractice calculations and into the E/M component of global surgical codes.

## What to bill instead, by setting

with reassigned billing rights. Rural Health Clinics and Federally Qualified Health Centers: consultation codes were discontinued in favor of office visit codes (99201-99215) and nursing facility codes (99304-99306) as appropriate. ## Documentation

All E/M services must meet existing E/M documentation guidelines. Services should be documented during or immediately after they are provided. Code selection should reflect the actual service content.

## Timeline

The effective date was January 1, 2010, and implementation was January 4, 2010. The transmittal removed all references to consultation codes from Claims Processing Manual Chapter 12, Section 30.6.

final_text:
**Most plausible reason code: CARC 181.** The project's paraphrase of it is "The procedure code wasn't valid on the date of service." Its project rule is `deprecated_code`. This match is my inference. No tool linked claim 1254448 to that rule directly.

**Why it fits:** The claim is an outpatient claim billed with HCPCS 99241, a consultation code. The CMS Transmittal 1875 summary says Medicare stopped recognizing consultation codes 99241-99245 for Part B payment on January 1, 2010. The policy documents don't name a CARC for this situation.

**The score:** The model gives a denial probability of 0.9518. The validation-set average is 0.1805, so this is 5.27 times the average, or 77.1 percentage points above it. The model weighs HCPCS_CD = 99241 most heavily, at 4.647 log-odds. That is an odds multiplier of 104.3, or a 10330 percent change in the odds. The principal diagnosis J029 adds only 0.114. I can't say what J029 means, because the project reference doesn't include it. The other features shown are small.

The model weighs the procedure code. It doesn't identify a reason code, and CARC 181 is my reading of the pattern. The denial label here is synthetic, so this is not a real payer decision.
